title: Moving on old stock
summary: Stock you cannot sell still has to go somewhere: TCG Card Shop Simulator defines a bulk donation box for cards, and packaged goods keep their own saved contents.
body: Cards you do not want to price can be handled in bulk rather than one at a time, which is why the game gives donations their own panel.
Boxes keep saved contents of their own, so a container is a place stock lives rather than a cosmetic prop.
Because containers and shelves are tracked separately, clearing space is a real job you do before the next delivery arrives.
The donation panel is built out of parts. It keeps a slot empty for adding a new card and shows a count group with its own text, which is why a bulk donation displays what is going in before it goes.
What this entry does not tell you: what a donation is worth, whether it affects customers, or how much a box holds. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: There is a bulk donation box for cards, with its own panel.
Packaged goods keep their own saved contents.
Boxes and shelves are tracked separately.
The bulk donation panel keeps an empty slot for adding a new card, a count group and a count text of its own.
Moving stock on is done through objects the build names for the job: a bulk donation box and a bin.
The build also ships its own rubbish bags and rubbish cans for clearing a shop out.
